facts.text: This is Civil Appeal No. 14 of 1963.

anchor.surface_text: Civil Appeal No. 14 of 1963.

facts.text: Appeal arises from judgment and decree dated July 30, 1962 of Rajasthan High Court in Civil Regular S.A. No. 223 of 1961.

anchor.surface_text: From the judgment and decree dated July 30, 1962, of the Rajasthan High Court in Civil Regular S. A. No. 223 of 1961.

facts.text: Judgment delivered on March 4, 1963 by GAJENDRAGADKAR J.

anchor.surface_text: 1963. March 4. The judgment of the companyrt was delivered by GAJENDRAGADKAR J.

facts.text: Appellant is tenant of premises in suit owned by respondent.

anchor.surface_text: The appellant is a tenant of the premises in suit which are owned by the respondent.

facts.text: Premises let out to appellant by respondent under rent-note executed on December 8, 1953.

anchor.surface_text: These premises were let out to the appellant by the respondent under a rent-note executed on December 8, 1953.

facts.text: Appellant permitted to use premises for his Oil Mill.

anchor.surface_text: The appellant was permitted to use the said premises for his Oil Mill.

facts.text: Lease stipulated period was five years.

anchor.surface_text: before the expiry of the stipulated period which was five years,

facts.text: Lease terms required appellant to pay agreed rent every month; default for three months entitled respondent to evict before expiry and claim remaining rent.

anchor.surface_text: The terms of the lease provided that the appellant was to pay to the respondent the agreed rent every month and in case of default for three months, the respondent was entitled to evict the appellant

facts.text: On May 2, 1959, respondent sued appellant for ejectment in Court of Munsif, East Jaipur City.

anchor.surface_text: On May 2, 1959, the respondent sued the appellant for ejectment in the Court of Munsif, East Jaipur City.

facts.text: Respondent alleged rent received from appellant up to October 31, 1957, thereafter default despite demands.

anchor.surface_text: He alleged that he had received the rent from the appellant up to October 31, 1957 and that thereafter the appellant had defaulted in the payment of rent in spite of repeated demands,

facts.text: Respondent alleged at suit date appellant in arrears of rent and failed to pay house tax per agreement.

anchor.surface_text: and that even at the date of the suit he was in arrears of rent and had failed to pay the house tax according to the agreement.

facts.text: Respondent's case: appellant's tenancy expired on December 1, 1958 by efflux of time but appellant failed to deliver possession.

anchor.surface_text: His case was that the appellants tenancy had expired on December 1, 1958 by efflux of time, but the appellant nevertheless failed to deliver over possession of the premises to the respondent.

facts.text: Appellant deposited lump sum of Rs. 1053/- to cover period from November 1, 1957 to November 30, 1958.

anchor.surface_text: He, however, purported to deposit a lump sum of Rs. 1053/- to companyer the period from November 1, 1957 to November 30, 1958 which was due from him.

facts.text: Respondent pleaded appellant committed more than three defaults in payment of rent of two months each during period of 18 months.

anchor.surface_text: The respondent pleaded that the appellant had companymitted more than three defaults in the payment of rent of two months each during the period of 18 months

facts.text: Respondent pleaded at date of suit rent or mesne profits for 5 months and 2 days remained unpaid.

anchor.surface_text: and that even -at the date of the suit, the rent or mesne profits for 5 months and 2 days still remained to be paid.

facts.text: Appellant denied respondent's claim for ejectment citing section 13(1)(a) of Rajasthan Premises Control of Rent and Eviction Act, 1950.

anchor.surface_text: The appellant denied the respondents claim and alleged that the respondent was number entitled to claim ejectment against him by virtue of the provisions of section 13 1  a  of the Rajasthan Premises  Control of Rent arid Eviction  Act, 1950  Act XVII of 1950   hereinafter called the Act .

facts.text: Appellant pleaded respondent accepted rent paid by appellant and waived right to evict; denied any default.

anchor.surface_text: He also pleaded that by virtue of the fact that the respondent had accepted rent paid by the appellant, he had waived his right to evict him. In other words, he denied that there was any default,

facts.text: At first hearing of suit in trial court, appellant deposited Rs. 648/- on account of rent due up to that date, accepted by respondent without prejudice.

anchor.surface_text: At the date of the first hearing of the suit in the trial Court, the appellant deposited Rs. 648/- on account of rent due up to the said date and the said payment was accepted by the respondent without prejudice.

facts.text: Trial court framed four issues, principal issue whether appellant committed three defaults of two months within 18 months in payment of rent.

anchor.surface_text: On these pleadings, the learned trial judge framed four issues, the principal issue being whether the appellant had companymitted three defaults of two months within the period of 18 months in the payment of rent ?

facts.text: Trial court found in favour of appellant on principal issue and other issues, dismissed respondent's suit.

anchor.surface_text: The finding of the trial Court on the said issue as well as on the other issues framed by it was in favour of the appellant. In the result, the respondents suit was dismissed.

facts.text: Respondent preferred appeal to Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Jaipur City.

anchor.surface_text: The respondent then preferred an appeal in the Court of the Additional Sessions Judge, Jaipur City.

facts.text: Appellate court held appellant committed three defaults on facts proved by respondent, entitled to ejectment decree; set aside trial court decree.

anchor.surface_text: The appellate Court held that on the facts proved by the respondent, the three defaults had been companymitted by the appellant, and so, he was entitled to a decree for ejectment. On these findings, the decree passed by the trial Court was set aside

facts.text: Appellant preferred second appeal before Rajasthan High Court.

anchor.surface_text: The appellant challenged this decision by preferring a second appeal before the Rajasthan High Court.

facts.text: Rajasthan High Court single judge dismissed second appeal.

anchor.surface_text: This appeal was heard by a learned single judge of the said High Court and was dismissed.

facts.text: Appellant's request for leave to appeal under Letters Patent rejected by High Court judge.

anchor.surface_text: The appellants request for leave to prefer an appeal under Letters Patent was rejected by the learned Judge.

facts.text: Appellant applied for and obtained special leave to appeal to Supreme Court against High Court single judge decision.

anchor.surface_text: It is against the decision of the learned single judge in second appeal that the appellant applied for and obtained special leave to appeal to this Court.
the respondents prayer that the special leave granted to the appellant should be revoked, is well-founded.
